newsitem.title: FRANCE: Michelin rises on Merrill upgrade.
newsitem.headline: Michelin rises on Merrill upgrade.

text.p: Shares in Michelin were up more than two percent on Monday after Merrill Lynch raised its recommendation on the stock to buy from hold, citing the steep decline in the tyremaker's heavy debt and improvements in its operating and financial performance.
The stock was up 6.5 francs, or 2.12 percent, at 313.10 francs at 1225 GMT, while the CAC index was up 0.3 percent.
Michelin shares have gone up 13 percent this year, helped by falling rubber prices and a rising dollar.

"Mention Michelin and many investors immediately envisage a pile of debt," Merrill Lynch said in a stock comment. "What the market is not discounting is how quickly Michelin is throwing off that debt burden," with a debt to equity ratio seen at 135 percent at the end of 1996 from 441 percent in 1993.
"The prospective estimated 1997 and 1998 ratings of nine times and 7.7 times (earnings) are 22 percent and 33 percent below Michelin's 11.5 times peak 1987 multiple," it said.
"Applying Michelin's 1987 multiple of 11.5 times to our forecast 1997 Michelin EPS gives us a price objective of 380 francs, or 27 percent above current levels," Merrill Lynch said.
Another industry analyst, however, said he was less bullish on Michelin's stock given the weakness in the European truck market which is more important in terms of margins for Michelin than volumes.
